answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each identity check to a challenge-derived sequence of modular squarings: each result feeds the next, imposing elapsed time that GPUs cannot parallelize within one instance. An attacker may run separate clones concurrently, but each requires its own sequential work, so identities cannot be created faster merely by splitting one computation. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently; canyon, horizon, and prism can label distinct challenge contexts without weakening this time bottleneck.
